props.title: Rock Star

sections.content: **Rock Star** (2001) captures the electric fantasy of an ordinary fan becoming a musical idol, following Mark Wahlberg as Chris Cole, a tribute band singer who gets to front the very metal band he worships. The film draws inspiration from the real story of Tim "Ripper" Owens, who joined Judas Priest after years in a tribute band. Like **Almost Famous** (2000) and **This Is Spinal Tap** (1984), it peels back the glossy veneer of rock stardom to reveal the messy humanity underneath. Director Stephen Herek brings the same energy he channeled in **Bill & Ted's Excellent Adventure** (1989) but adds a darker edge exploring fame's toll.

sections.content: The early 2000s saw a revival of rock-focused films that balanced nostalgia with critical examination of the genre's excesses. **Velvet Goldmine** (1998) dove into glam rock's theatrical heights, while **What We Do Is Secret** (2007) captured punk's raw energy through the story of The Germs. **Rock Star** fits perfectly in this period, celebrating metal's theatrical bombast while acknowledging its limitations and casualties. SUBHEAD: The Price of Fame Theme in Rock Films

The "overnight success" narrative gets particularly compelling treatment in music films of this era. **That Thing You Do!** (1996) showed the dizzying rise and fall of a one-hit-wonder band, while **Eddie and the Cruisers** (1983) explored the dark side of rock mythology. **Rock Star** shares DNA with these films but adds specific commentary on fan culture and authenticity in metal music, themes that would later resurface in **Metal Lords** (2022) and **Lords of Chaos** (2018).
